axes.axis: 2. fence-before-CAS ordering -- no-op at fence with a stale row version; stale-replay refusal; can a stale replay slip past the CAS?
axes.verdict: PASS on correctness; FAIL on proof (see RE-1)
correctness: Read order in campaignSourceMaterialization.ts: SELECT (:73-81) -> row-absent conflict (:82-86) -> fence equality noop (:89-91) -> fence-behind refusal (:92-94) -> version CAS (:97-99) -> UPDATE with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?` (:104-112) -> `changes === 0` conflict (:114-116).

No-op with a stale row version: the fence branch returns at :90 before :97 is evaluated, so a replay standing AT the fence is a silent no-op whatever version it carries. CORRECT. NOT COVERED BY ANY ROW -- see RE-1.

Stale-replay refusal: :93 returns before :97, so a replay standing BEHIND the fence is `refused` and never writes, whatever version it carries. CORRECT. Row (c) proves the refusal but only with a current version.

Can a stale replay slip past the CAS in any interleaving? NO. The decision is taken on a possibly-stale read, but the UPDATE re-asserts the predicate in SQL (`AND version = ?`). Any concurrent materialization that advanced the fence also advanced the version -- they are written in one statement (:104-112) -- so fence-advance implies version-advance implies `changes === 0` implies `conflict`. A concurrent whole-envelope PUT likewise bumps `version`. There is no interleaving in which a caller at-or-behind the stored fence writes the row, and none in which a caller ahead of the fence overwrites a row that moved under it.

The redundant-in-transaction SQL predicate is correctly kept and correctly justified at :110-112: outside the borrowed-handle transaction (the future replay driver) it is the only thing standing between the read and the write.

axes.axis: 3c. withoutClientFence strips client-sent fences before persist -- a client can never set or advance it
evidence: `stored` is built as `{ ...withoutClientFence(prepared.record), version: nextVersion, ...(storedFence === null ? {} : { sourceReplayFence: storedFence }) }` -- CampaignPersistenceService.ts:161-166.
`withoutClientFence` copies and deletes the key (campaignSourceMaterialization.ts:129-135), so whatever the client sent is gone before the re-stamp.

The re-stamped value is `storedFence`, read from the ROW (:145-146), never from the envelope. A client cannot set a fence on an unfenced row (stripped, and the conditional spread adds nothing) and cannot advance one on a fenced row (the guard demands exact equality first, then the write re-stamps the stored value). Only `materializeCampaignSourceRow` advances it.
Row (d) pins the negative half: after a successful saveCampaign on an unfenced row, `recordOf(after).sourceReplayFence` is undefined (test:352).

axes.axis: 3d. A PUT to a NEVER-materialized row is byte-identical to today
axes.verdict: PASS behaviourally, with a partial pin
reasoning: `storedFence === null` makes the guard inert (:147) and the conditional spread contribute nothing (:165).

Key order is unchanged: `{ ...record }` preserves the source object's own-enumerable key order, `delete` of an absent key is a no-op, and re-assigning `version` after the spread overwrites in place rather than moving the key. `JSON.stringify` therefore emits the same bytes as the pre-commit `{ ...prepared.record, version: nextVersion }`.

ONE deliberate behaviour change on this path: before the commit a client-injected `sourceReplayFence` would have been persisted (hydrate/migrate pass extra keys through); now it is stripped. That is a strict improvement, not a regression.

evidence: Route: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:590-604. `materializeCampaignSourceRow` runs inside the `extend` callback, AFTER `append()` returned `committed`, on the SAME `db` handle.

contractFor64: WHERE THE ECHO MUST COME FROM. `buildSerializedCampaign` (src/lib/campaign/persistence/campaignEnvelope.ts:32-52) builds the PUT envelope field-by-field from a live `ICampaign` and has no fence field. 6.4 must thread the stored fence in -- most naturally as an extra optional member of the existing `identity` argument, which is already the 'server-owned facts the client echoes' slot alongside instanceId/authority.

WHERE IT MUST BE REMEMBERED. `metadataFrom` (src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:492-501) projects the server record into `ICampaignSaveMetadata` and drops the fence. 6.4 must add a field there (or a sibling store slot) and populate it from EVERY server record the client sees: load, save-ok, AND the 409 `current`.

THE ONE THAT WILL BITE. `resolveConflictTakeServerAction` (:1191-1219) is the UI's recovery from a 409: it adopts `conflictServerRecord` but rebuilds metadata through `metadataFrom`, so the fence is dropped again and the next save is 409'd identically. Until 6.4 carries the fence through THIS path, 'take server' does not clear a fence conflict and the campaign becomes unsaveable from the UI. Auto-save is at least not a hot loop -- `armAutoSaveTimer` (:972-980) returns early while saveState === 'conflict'.

DO NOT DISCRIMINATE ON THE VERSION. The 409 body always carries `reason: 'base-state-unavailable'` and `currentVersion: result.current.version` (src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts:216-222). In a PURE fence refusal `currentVersion` EQUALS the client's own `baseVersion` -- the CAS would have passed.
